messages:
raj: compliance alert: recent snapshot uploads for tenant-99 showing SSE-S3 (not CMEK) in S3 inventory. looks like some uploads bypassed CMEK enforcement
emily: ack. i saw an alarm too when automated audit found objects without x-amz-server-side-encryption:aws:kms header
tony: quick forensics: upload logs show PutObject succeeded but KMS CloudTrail records show `Encrypt` denied for principal arn:aws:iam::123:role/snapshot-uploader at 23:12:01Z
raj: exact KMS error from uploader: `AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Encrypt on key arn:aws:kms:...:key/zz99`
backup-watch: i parsed recent key-policy changes: PR 621 modified key policy for key/zz99 to remove a broad statement (leftover from onboarding) and added a `Condition` restricting `kms:Encrypt` to `aws:SourceAccount` — unintentionally excluded the uploader role which assumes a cross-account role
emily: can we quickly narrow-scope mitigation? options: 1) restore previous policy 2) add explicit statement permitting snapshot-uploader role 3) apply S3 bucket-level enforcement to reject non-CMEK uploads
ton: emergency fix: i patched key policy to re-add explicit `Allow` for `arn:aws:iam::123:role/snapshot-uploader` with `kms:Encrypt` and `kms:GenerateDataKey*` and re-run a test upload — now PutObject shows SSE-KMS header and encrypt logs OK :white_check_mark:
raj: good. forensics: query i ran against CloudTrail: `fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters.keyId, errorMessage | filter eventName = "Encrypt" and requestParameters.keyId = "arn:aws:kms:...:key/zz99"`
emily: follow-ups: 1) run an inventory for last 72h to find objects without `x-amz-server-side-encryption` and re-encrypt or re-upload 2) add pre-merge CI guard: if a PR alters KMS key policy, require owner review + integration test that exercises cross-account roles 3) add S3 bucket policy to enforce `sse:kms` for PutObject and deny if missing
backup-watch: quick scan found ~18 objects from two snapshots uploaded during the outage window — submitting retention and re-encryption job now. will push to ticket link: https://tickets/redwood/SEC-431
oncall-sre: consider also adding a short-lived detector: alert if PutObject without SSE-KMS spikes >3/min for a bucket
ton: also note: snapshot-uploader should log the exact KMS error and the key ARN in metrics so we can auto-triage similar issues earlier
raj: i'll write the postmortem blurb and timeline. probable root cause: key-policy tightening combined with cross-account assumption not considered in PR. will include remediation checklist
sec-bot: Incident recorded (id=sec-2026-03-21-11). Reminder: attach CloudTrail snippets, S3 manifests, and the modified policy diff to the ticket for audit
emily: leaving this thread open 48h for any late evidence and to confirm re-encrypt job completes successfully
